title: Randomized-controlled evaluation of an online navigation tool for people with mental disorders
summary:
A wide range of medical, psychosocial, and rehabilitation services is available within the German mental health care system for people experiencing mental health problems, including counselling services, outpatient psychotherapy, and rehabilitation programmes. However, the diversity of available services makes the system difficult to navigate. In addition, some services are difficult to access or have limited availability. As a result, people may receive appropriate support too late or access services that do not adequately meet their needs, increasing the risk that mental health problems become chronic and place a greater burden on those affected.
The aim of the NaMeCa project is to develop an automated digital care navigator that supports people with mental health problems in identifying appropriate medical and psychosocial services according to their individual needs and facilitates access to the mental health care system.
The present study focuses on the scientific evaluation of the automated digital care navigator. In a randomized controlled trial the study will investigate whether the automated digital care navigator improves navigation within the mental health care system, increases knowledge of available support services, facilitates dealing with barriers to care, and is perceived by users as helpful and usable.

interventions.name: The intervention group (IG) receives immediate access to the online care navigator. Assessments are conducted at baseline T0 (after eligibility criteria have been met), followed immediately by randomisation, at T1 (6 weeks after randomisation) and at T2 (26 weeks after randomisation).
The waitlist control group (CG) receives delayed access to the care navigator (26 weeks after randomisation). Assessment time points are identical to those of the intervention group.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Self-reported mental health problems or a mental disorder
- Relevant experiences were made in Germany, i.e. within the German health care system
- Internet access and a valid email address
Exclusion criteria:
- Persons not meeting the inclusion criteria
- Persons who do not provide informed consent, do not agree to the data protection terms, or withdraw their consent
